sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This past fall, 200 people gathered at the Explorers Club in New York City.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，200人聚集在纽约市的探险家俱乐部。

sentences.en: The building was once a clubhouse to famed naturalists and explorers.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑曾是著名自然主义者和探险家们的俱乐部。

sentences.en: Now it's an archive of ephemera and rarities from pioneering expeditions,
sentences.zh: 如今，它成了先锋探险活动中各种临时物件和珍稀文物的档案馆，

sentences.en: from treks to the world's tallest mountains, the North Pole, and the moon.
sentences.zh: 从世界最高峰、北极到月球的远征。

sentences.en: Woolly mammoth tusks frame a fireplace.
sentences.zh: 长毛猛犸象的牙齿装点着壁炉的外框。

sentences.en: A menacing polar bear towers near the landing with claws at the ready.
sentences.zh: 一只极具压迫感的北极熊在楼梯平台附近昂然挺立，利爪蓄势待发。

sentences.en: And a cheetah, rumored to have been shot by Teddy Roosevelt, sits on a plinth just upstairs.
sentences.zh: 而在楼上的基座上，还摆着一只据说是西奥多·罗斯福射杀的猎豹。

sentences.en: The gathering was in honor of a new expedition.
sentences.zh: 这次聚会是为了纪念一次新的探险。

sentences.en: One in search, not of a single animal, but of thousands.
sentences.zh: 这次寻找的不是某一种动物，而是数千只。

sentences.en: That's reporter Caitlin Swaljay.
sentences.zh: 这位是记者凯特琳·斯瓦尔杰。

sentences.en: The club was hosting a biological census.
sentences.zh: 俱乐部正在主办一场生物普查。

sentences.en: An ecological survey so difficult, so complicated, so taxing,
sentences.zh: 这是一项极其困难、极其复杂、极其繁重的生态调查，

sentences.en: that it had never been attempted before, and may never be attempted again.
sentences.zh: 以往从未有人尝试过，也可能不会再有第二次。

sentences.en: It is a really big project.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个大项目。

sentences.en: Like, I don't think we've ever been involved in a project of this scope in our lives.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们一生中从未参与过如此规模的项目。

sentences.en: It's like moving a small little army around.
sentences.zh: 就像调动一支小型军队一样。

sentences.en: This is Jamie Allen.
sentences.zh: 这位是杰米·艾伦。

sentences.en: The census was his idea.
sentences.zh: 这场普查是他的主意。

sentences.en: And when he started, it was a small operation.
sentences.zh: 当他刚开始时，这只是一项小规模的操作。

sentences.en: But now Jamie is merely the tip of a vast pyramid of census-related personnel,
sentences.zh: 但现在，杰米仅仅是庞大普查人员金字塔的冰山一角，

sentences.en: including a logistics chief, a chief cartographer, a veterinarian, an epidemiologist,
sentences.zh: 其中包括后勤主管、首席制图师、兽医、流行病学家、

sentences.en: a specialist from the Fish and Wildlife Service, and of course, a web team.
sentences.zh: 鱼类及野生动物管理局的专家，当然，还有网络团队。

sentences.en: And that's just the core staff.
sentences.zh: 这还只是核心员工。

sentences.en: Below them are the foot soldiers, the volunteers who must go out into the field and do the actual counting.
sentences.zh: 在他们下面是底层士兵，也就是必须深入实地进行实际清点的志愿者。

sentences.en: 300-plus volunteers counting 700 hectares, 100 meter by 100 meter,
sentences.zh: 300多名志愿者清点700公顷的土地，每块100米乘以100米，

sentences.en: and 3,000-plus sheets of paper that we have to—it's—yeah.
sentences.zh: 还有3000多页纸我们需要——这——是的。

sentences.en: A vast filing system, multiple offices, and a team of hundreds,
sentences.zh: 庞大的归档系统、多个办公室，以及一个由数百人组成的团队，

sentences.en: all for the sake of answering one question.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了回答一个问题。

sentences.en: I want to know how many squirrels are in Central Park.
sentences.zh: 我想知道中央公园里有多少只松鼠。

sentences.en: Squirrels.
sentences.zh: 松鼠。

sentences.en: They're counting squirrels.
sentences.zh: 他们在数松鼠。

sentences.en: Date, October 14th, 2018.
Time, 526.
sentences.zh: 时间，5点26分。

sentences.en: On a chilly Sunday evening, I'm following Stu,
sentences.zh: 在一个寒冷的周日傍晚，我跟着斯图，

sentences.en: one of the Central Park census volunteers, around the park's northern end.
sentences.zh: 他是中央公园普查的志愿者之一，在公园北端四处走动。

sentences.en: We're on the hunt for eastern grey squirrels, which is like THE squirrel.
sentences.zh: 我们在搜寻东灰松鼠，也就是那种“正宗”的松鼠。

sentences.en: It's what you'll find in just about any American city, but especially Central Park.
sentences.zh: 你在几乎任何美国城市都能见到它，但在中央公园尤其多。

sentences.en: So we need to be on this path down here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要走这条小路。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How do we get in here?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么进去？

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to—I'll pretend you're not here, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要——我假装你不在，好吗？

sentences.en: I just keep doing it.
sentences.zh: 我只管继续。

sentences.en: All right, cool.
sentences.zh: 好吧，酷。

sentences.en: Following his lead, we head off the path, over fences and through tall brush.
sentences.zh: 顺着他的带领，我们离开小路，翻过栅栏，穿过高高的灌木丛。

sentences.en: My face is going to be covered in poison ivies, too.
sentences.zh: 我的脸也快沾满毒常春藤了。

sentences.en: Oh, God, without a doubt.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: We're slowly making our way to his designated area, hectare 38E.
sentences.zh: 我们正慢慢前往他被分配的区域，38E公顷。

sentences.en: Hectares are plots of land that measure a little less than two and a half acres each.
sentences.zh: 公顷是面积略小于两英亩半的土地。

sentences.en: The job of a census volunteer is to count all the squirrels they can find within their assigned hectares
sentences.zh: 普查志愿者的工作是清点他们所分配的公顷内能找到的所有松鼠，

sentences.en: and only their assigned hectares.
sentences.zh: 而且只能数他们分配的公顷。

sentences.en: Although this doesn't stop Stu from getting incredibly excited by every squirrel he sees.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并不能阻止斯图对看到的每一只松鼠兴奋不已。

sentences.en: Oh, look, there's a squirrel.
sentences.zh: 哦，看，有一只松鼠。

sentences.en: I can't count you, buddy.
sentences.zh: 我不能数你，老兄。

sentences.en: You're not in my hectare.
sentences.zh: 你不在我的公顷里。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 走吧。

sentences.en: Back.
sentences.zh: 回去。

sentences.en: See you later.
sentences.zh: 回见。

sentences.en: After every hectare in the park has been surveyed, all the data will get plugged into
sentences.zh: 公园里的每一个公顷都被调查完之后，所有的数据将被输入

sentences.en: a wildlife counting formula popularized by the great mid-century Danish-American squirrel
sentences.zh: 一个由20世纪中叶伟大的丹麦裔美籍松鼠生物学家冯·弗利格

sentences.en: biologist, Von Flieger.
sentences.zh: 普及的野生动物计数公式中。

sentences.en: The formula will account for squirrels that were double-counted and ones no one managed to
sentences.zh: 该公式将核算重复计数的松鼠以及任何人都没能找到的松鼠，

sentences.en: find, and then finally spit out a number that the world has been waiting for.
sentences.zh: 最后吐出一个全世界都在等待的数字。

sentences.en: The squirrel abundance number.
sentences.zh: 松鼠丰度数字。

sentences.en: At which point you would be totally justified in asking, as many do, what precisely is the
sentences.zh: 这时候你完全有理由像许多人一样发问：确切地说，

sentences.en: point in knowing the squirrel abundance number?
sentences.zh: 知道松鼠的丰度数字有什么意义？

sentences.en: What they're saying is, like, you're counting squirrels?
sentences.zh: 他们说的是，你们在数松鼠吗？

sentences.en: Like, squirrels have a specific context in people's minds, and it's to be ignored.
sentences.zh: 松鼠在人们心中有一种既定的印象，那就是被忽视。

sentences.en: Like, it's assumed, I think, that because they're so common, we know everything we need to know
sentences.zh: 我想，由于它们太常见了，大家会觉得我们已经掌握了关于松鼠所需了解的一切。

sentences.en: about squirrels.
sentences.zh: 关于松鼠的。

sentences.en: But the opposite's true.
sentences.zh: 但事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The very fact that no one has bothered to do a Central Park squirrel census before to gather
sentences.zh: 正因为以前从来没有人费心去对中央公园进行松鼠普查，来收集关于我们景观中最常见动物之一的最基础数据点，

sentences.en: this most basic of data points about one of the most common animals in our landscape reveals a
sentences.zh: 关于我们周围最常见动物之一的这一最基础的数据点，揭示了

sentences.en: kind of societal blind spot we have in regard to squirrels.
sentences.zh: 这暴露出我们在对待松鼠时的一种社会盲区。

sentences.en: For a long time now, we've taken them for granted, including the story of where all these squirrels
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，我们把它们视为理所当然，包括所有这些松鼠的来源故事。

sentences.en: came from.
sentences.zh: 从何而来。

sentences.en: The squirrels we see in our cities and towns are so everyday, so ubiquitous, so just there,
sentences.zh: 我们在城市和小镇里看到的松鼠是那么日常、那么无处不在、那么自然而然，

sentences.en: that it's easy to assume they've always been there.
sentences.zh: 以至于很容易让人觉得它们一直就在那里。

sentences.en: But the truth is, they haven't.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Mid-19th century, you could walk through a place like Boston or Philadelphia or Manhattan,
sentences.zh: 19世纪中期，如果你走在波士顿、费城或曼哈顿这样的地方，

sentences.en: and you would not see a single squirrel.
sentences.zh: 你一只松鼠也见不到。

sentences.en: This is Etienne Benson.
sentences.zh: 这位是埃蒂安·本森。

sentences.en: He's a historian of environmental science at the University of Pennsylvania, and he says
sentences.zh: 他是宾夕法尼亚大学的环境科学历史学家，他说

sentences.en: the cities of the early 19th century were effectively squirrel-less.
sentences.zh: 19世纪早期的城市实际上是没有松鼠的。

sentences.en: These were animals you could only see if you left the city.
sentences.zh: 这些只有当你离开城市时才能见到的动物。

sentences.en: And then even perhaps left the farm, right, and went deep into the woods.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能还要离开农场，对吧，深入森林。

sentences.en: And it was only when you went deep into the woods that you would have the chance to see
sentences.zh: 只有当你深入森林时，你才有可能

sentences.en: something like a squirrel.
sentences.zh: 看到像松鼠这样的东西。

sentences.en: In fact, squirrels were considered so elusive that the very wealthy liked to keep them
sentences.zh: 事实上，松鼠曾被认为极其难得，以至于大富大贵之人喜欢把它们

sentences.en: as exotic pets.
sentences.zh: 当作异国宠物养着。

sentences.en: In 1856, an article in the New York Times described how one such pet escaped from its owner's home
sentences.zh: 1856年，《纽约时报》的一篇文章描述了一只这样的宠物如何从它在曼哈顿的主人家中逃脱，

sentences.en: in Manhattan, and when it was discovered in a tree, a crowd of people gathered in amazement
sentences.zh: 当它被发现在一棵树上时，一大群人惊叹不已地聚集在一起，

sentences.en: trying to lure it down.
sentences.zh: 试图把它诱哄下来。

sentences.en: Eventually, the crowd grew so large and rowdy that the police had to forcibly disperse it.
sentences.zh: 最终，人群变得如此庞大和喧闹，以至于警察不得不出面强行驱散。

sentences.en: So how did these eastern gray squirrels, these reclusive woodland creatures, make their way
sentences.zh: 那么这些东灰松鼠，这些隐居的森林生物，是如何进入

sentences.en: into our urban spaces?
sentences.zh: 我们的城市空间的呢？

sentences.en: Well, for starters, says Etienne, they didn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，埃蒂安说，它们并没有自己来。

sentences.en: At least not on their own.
sentences.zh: 至少不是靠它们自己。

sentences.en: What was so fascinating to me was to find out that they had been intentionally introduced.
sentences.zh: 最让我着迷的是发现它们是被故意引进的。

sentences.en: The squirrels that we all take for granted as we walk through the park or on our way to the gym
sentences.zh: 我们穿过公园、走在去健身房或办公室的路上时觉得理所当然的松鼠，

sentences.en: or the office are only there because we put them there.
sentences.zh: 之所以在那里，完全是因为我们把它们放那儿的。

sentences.en: They were deliberately brought into cities and fed and sheltered.
sentences.zh: 它们是被蓄意带进城市的，并得到了喂养和庇护。

sentences.en: The first city that we know of to introduce squirrels was Philadelphia in 1847.
sentences.zh: 我们所知的第一个引入松鼠的城市是1847年的费城。

sentences.en: Like many East Coast cities of the mid-19th century, it was already a highly urban environment.
sentences.zh: 就像19世纪中期的许多东海岸城市一样，它已经是一个高度城市化的环境。

sentences.en: People yearned for a taste of the wilderness that the squirrel was seen to embody.
sentences.zh: 人们渴望体验松鼠身上所体现的荒野气息。

sentences.en: They were captured in the wilderness, brought into the city, and placed on a single tree,
sentences.zh: 它们在野外被捕获，带进城市，并被安置在一棵树上，

sentences.en: almost as if they were animals in a menagerie or a zoo.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像它们是动物园或兽栏里的动物一样。

sentences.en: The tree was in the middle of a small public square, and it was equipped with a wooden shelter
sentences.zh: 这棵树在一个小公共广场的正中央，它配备了一个木制避难所

sentences.en: and a fence so the squirrels could stay safe from the elements and any would-be predators
sentences.zh: 和一个栅栏，这样松鼠们就能在它们的小松鼠之家里

sentences.en: in their little squirrel home.
sentences.zh: 免受恶劣天气和任何潜在捕食者的侵害。

sentences.en: A few other cities, like Boston, replicated this model.
sentences.zh: 其他一些城市，比如波士顿，也复制了这种模式。

sentences.en: And at first, the number of squirrels was teeny tiny.
sentences.zh: 起初，松鼠的数量非常少。

sentences.en: Philadelphia started out with only three.
sentences.zh: 费城一开始只有三只。

sentences.en: Think of it as a trial run.
sentences.zh: 把它当成一次试运行。

sentences.en: Only this first trial run?
sentences.zh: 只是这第一次试运行呢？

sentences.en: It went terribly.
sentences.zh: 进展得糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: When I started working on this topic, I thought,
sentences.zh: 当我开始研究这个课题时，我想，

sentences.en: OK, you introduce a few squirrels into an urban park,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你把几只松鼠引入城市公园，

sentences.en: in a few years you're going to have thousands of squirrels, no problem.
sentences.zh: 几年后你就会有几千只松鼠，没问题。

sentences.en: But at the very beginning, they were essentially incapable of surviving.
sentences.zh: 但一开始，它们基本上不具备生存能力。

sentences.en: The cities of the 19th century just didn't have the kind of large parks
sentences.zh: 19世纪的城市根本没有我们今天看到的那种大型公园

sentences.en: and extensive tree cover we see today.
sentences.zh: 和广阔的树木覆盖率。

sentences.en: When you thought about urban landscapes,
sentences.zh: 当你想到城市景观时，

sentences.en: they were very unfriendly to an animal that required trees for food.
sentences.zh: 它们对需要树木来获取食物的动物非常不友好。

sentences.en: In the classic storybook image of a squirrel, it's always clutching an acorn.
sentences.zh: 在童话书里松鼠的经典形象中，它总是紧紧抓着一颗橡果。

sentences.en: And that's basically true.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是真的。

sentences.en: A wild squirrel requires deciduous, nut-bearing plants, such as oak trees, in order to survive.
sentences.zh: 野生松鼠需要落叶植物、产坚果的植物（如橡树）才能生存。

sentences.en: Without trees, the city had to provide for the squirrels.
sentences.zh: 没有树木，城市就必须为松鼠提供给养。

sentences.en: But the squirrel feed often proved to be either insufficient or nutritionally worthless.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，松鼠的饲料往往要么不够，要么毫无营养价值。

sentences.en: So those first squirrels either died off, were killed, or were adopted as pets.
sentences.zh: 所以那些最早的松鼠要么死掉了，要么被杀了，要么被当成宠物收养了。

sentences.en: In 1855, a reporter for the Boston Evening Transcript described the introduction of squirrels
sentences.zh: 1855年，《波士顿晚报》的一位记者将松鼠的引进

sentences.en: as, quote, an absurd and reprehensible experiment.
sentences.zh: 描述为“荒谬且应受谴责的实验”。

sentences.en: All of which raises a question.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都引发了一个问题。

sentences.en: Why are there now squirrels everywhere in American cities?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在美国城市的到处都是松鼠？

sentences.en: I think it's more a model of, if you build it, they will come.
sentences.zh: 我认为这更符合“你若建好，它们就会到来”的模式。

sentences.en: Gabriel Willow is a naturalist who specializes in animal species that live in urban environments.
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔·威洛是一位专注于生活在城市环境中的动物物种的自然主义者。

sentences.en: So I study nature and educate people about the natural world, specifically in New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以我研究自然并向人们普及自然世界，特别是在纽约市。

sentences.en: And he says that in the late 19th century, green spaces like New York's were undergoing a transformation.
sentences.zh: 他说，在19世纪后期，像纽约这样的绿地正在经历一场转型。

sentences.en: Areas of open land, once multipurpose fields used for everything from cattle grazing to slaughterhouses and militia training,
sentences.zh: 曾经的多功能开阔地，从牛群放牧到屠宰场和民兵训练什么都用，

sentences.en: were being transformed into spaces of leisure.
sentences.zh: 正被转变为休闲空间。

sentences.en: And by the 1870s, city dwellers were leaving behind small, busy squares in favor of large, idyllic parks.
sentences.zh: 到1870年代，城市居民开始抛弃狭小拥挤的广场，转而前往大型、田园般的公园。

sentences.en: And although they were designed for people, these new urban oases just might be the best thing to ever happen to the eastern gray squirrel.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些公园是为人类设计的，但这些新兴的城市绿洲可能恰恰是东灰松鼠遇到的最好的事情。

sentences.en: Because the parks weren't just big.
sentences.zh: 因为这些公园不仅很大。

sentences.en: They were also designed to mimic the natural world.
sentences.zh: 它们的设计也是为了模仿自然界。

sentences.en: Take Central Park and Prospect Park in New York, for example, both designed by Calvert Vox and Frederick Law Olmstead.
sentences.zh: 以纽约的中央公园和展望公园为例，它们都是由卡尔弗特·沃克斯和弗雷德里克·劳·奥姆斯特德设计的。
zh_words: 弗雷德里克·劳·奥姆斯特德

sentences.en: They were working with the existing geology and hydrology.
sentences.zh: 他们利用了现有的地质和水文条件。

sentences.en: They took naturally existing small ponds or marshy areas and made lakes out of them.
sentences.zh: 他们将天然存在的小池塘或沼泽地改造成了湖泊。

sentences.en: They also chose to keep the area's dramatic rocky outcroppings, instead of blasting them away, as had been done with the rest of the city's grid.
sentences.zh: 他们还选择保留该地区引人注目的岩石露头，而不是像城市其他网格化区域那样将其炸毁。

sentences.en: And so they were working with certain natural elements.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们是在顺应某些自然元素进行设计。

sentences.en: These natural parks were filled with hedges and lakes and streams and lots and lots of trees,
sentences.zh: 这些自然公园里长满了树篱、湖泊、溪流，还有数不清的树木，

sentences.zh: 给城市生态带来了深远的影响。

sentences.en: In Europe, they're officially an invasive species.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都始于19世纪。

sentences.en: But even as American squirrels were taking out shopping malls and stock exchanges and invading
sentences.zh: 这就是自然适应人类城市的方式。

sentences.en: foreign countries, the very things that allowed them to proliferate in the first place were
sentences.zh: 在国外，正是那些曾经让他们数量激增的事物

sentences.en: slowly being taken away.
sentences.zh: 正在慢慢被剥夺。

sentences.en: Starting in the mid-20th century, ecologists, wildlife managers, and park officials started
sentences.zh: 从20世纪中期开始，生态学家、野生动物管理者和公园官员开始

sentences.en: to re-examine America's approach to wildlife.
sentences.zh: 重新审视美国对待野生动物的方式。

sentences.en: They began to argue that predators like coyotes and hawks should no longer be hunted for the
sentences.zh: 他们开始提出，为了人类以外的整个社群，

sentences.en: sake of a more-than-human community.
sentences.zh: 不应该再猎杀土狼和鹰之类的掠食者。

sentences.en: That starts to get replaced with a really different view, right, this ecological view in which we
sentences.zh: 这种观念开始被一种截然不同的观点所取代，对吧，这种生态学观点认为

sentences.en: understand those relationships of predation as essential to the ecosystem as a whole.
sentences.zh: 我们将这些捕食关系视为整个生态系统不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: In this new ecological model, the ideal environment was no longer one that corresponded to notions
sentences.zh: 在这种新的生态模型中，理想的环境不再对应着

sentences.en: of civilized versus uncivilized species, but one in which a variety of species, predator and
sentences.zh: 文明物种与未开化物种之分的观念，而是一个各种物种——无论是掠食者还是

sentences.en: prey alike, maintained a natural population balance with only minimal human intervention.
sentences.zh: 猎物——都能在仅需极少人类干预的情况下维持自然种群平衡的环境。

sentences.en: It took a few decades for this idea to spread from the national parks into the cities, but
sentences.zh: 这个想法从国家公园传播到城市花了几十年时间，但

sentences.en: by the 1980s, it had arrived, along with the predators.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪80年代，它伴随着掠食者一起到来了。

sentences.en: Which for an ecologically-minded naturalist like Gabriel Willow is a wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 对于像加布里埃尔·威洛这样具有生态意识的自然主义者来说，这绝对是一件美妙的事。

sentences.en: The coyotes are coming back on their own.
sentences.zh: 土狼正在自行回归。

sentences.en: We're not bringing them back.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有把它们带回来。

sentences.en: Ravens, ravens are nesting in New York City within the last 15 years.
sentences.zh: 乌鸦，乌鸦在过去15年里开始在纽约市筑巢。

sentences.en: We did not reintroduce them.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有重新引入它们。

sentences.en: The red-tailed hawk came back of its own accord.
sentences.zh: 红尾鹰也是自行回归的。

sentences.en: Other species we intentionally reintroduced, like peregrine falcons, and they're thriving.
sentences.zh: 其他物种则是我们有意重新引入的，比如游隼，它们现在长势喜人。

sentences.en: New York City has the highest population density of peregrine falcons in the world.
sentences.zh: 纽约市是世界上游隼种群密度最高的城市。

sentences.en: For most of us, the death of a few squirrels seems like a small price to pay in exchange
sentences.zh: 对我们大多数人来说，死几只松鼠似乎是用以换取

sentences.en: for this newfound biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 这种新发现的生物多样性的微小代价。

sentences.en: Today, there's no shortage of webcams, set up by people who have discovered a hawk's
sentences.zh: 如今，到处都是网络摄像头，它们由那些发现

sentences.en: nest outside their 12th floor apartment window.
sentences.zh: 12楼公寓窗外有鹰巢的人们架设。

sentences.en: And while we've been busy welcoming the squirrels' predators back into our cities, we've also
sentences.zh: 正当我们忙着迎接松鼠的天敌重返城市时，我们也

sentences.en: begun to finally withdraw our charity.
sentences.zh: 终于开始收回我们的慈悲。

sentences.en: I think everybody should go check out squirrels.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人都应该去看看松鼠。

sentences.en: They're pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 它们挺酷的。

sentences.en: I'm pro squirrel.
sentences.zh: 我是支持松鼠派的。

sentences.en: I'm team squirrel, you know.
sentences.zh: 我是松鼠战队的，你知道的。

sentences.en: I just don't think we need to be feeding them.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得我们没必要喂它们。

sentences.en: Gabriel and other naturalists think feeding squirrels has no place in the new ecological
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔和其他自然主义者认为，喂食松鼠在新的生态

sentences.en: model.
sentences.zh: 模型中没有立足之地。

sentences.en: Providing bread and other unnatural foods can lead to a variety of health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 提供面包和其他非天然食物会导致各种健康问题。

sentences.en: And acclimating squirrels to hand-feeding can make them overly dependent on humans, and
sentences.zh: 让松鼠习惯人工喂养会使它们过度依赖人类，

sentences.en: possibly prone to unstable population booMs.
sentences.zh: 并可能导致种群数量出现不稳定的暴涨。

sentences.en: None of which is ultimately good for the squirrels, or the larger environment.
sentences.zh: 这些对松鼠或更大的环境来说，最终都是有害无益的。

sentences.en: Which is why, 142 years after welcoming squirrels into the fold of our more-than-human community,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，在将松鼠纳入我们人类以外的社群142年之后，

sentences.en: New York City is done giving handouts.
sentences.zh: 纽约市不再提供免费施舍了。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Today is March 1st, 2019, and the time is 12.05.
sentences.zh: 今天是2019年3月1日，时间是12点05分。

sentences.en: Welcome to Pelham Fritz Recreation Center.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到佩勒姆·弗里茨康乐中心。

sentences.en: This past winter, the New York City Parks Department held a hearing for a proposed rule change
sentences.zh: 去年冬天，纽约市公园管理局就一项拟议的规则修改举行了听证会，

sentences.en: that would make it illegal to feed any wild animal in the parks.
sentences.zh: 该修改将使在公园里喂食任何野生动物的行为成为违法。

sentences.en: This hearing is intended to solicit comments regarding the proposed rule changes.
sentences.zh: 本次听证会旨在征求对拟议规则修改的意见。

sentences.en: These comments will become part of the public record.
sentences.zh: 这些意见将成为公共记录的一部分。

sentences.en: Gabriel Willow was there, too.
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔·威洛也在场。

sentences.en: Although it didn't go down quite the way he thought it would.
sentences.zh: 尽管事情的发展并不完全如他所料。

sentences.en: I didn't really expect it to be quite as skewed as it was in terms of almost everybody
sentences.zh: 我真没想到情况会这么一边倒，几乎

sentences.en: there was speaking against the regulations.
sentences.zh: 在场的每个人都在发言反对这些规章。

sentences.en: It's a criminal act that runs against the morals and rules of a civilized society.
sentences.zh: 这是一种违背文明社会道德和规则的犯罪行为。

sentences.en: New York Park says that the squirrels, they should be squirrels, they should be animals,
sentences.zh: 纽约公园表示，松鼠就应该是松鼠，就应该是动物，

sentences.en: and forage like they do in the wild.
sentences.zh: 像在野外一样自己觅食。

sentences.en: Except for one thing.
sentences.zh: 但有一点除外。

sentences.en: The parks aren't the wild.
sentences.zh: 公园可不是野外。

sentences.en: I don't know that I've encountered that many squirrel and pigeon feeding fans in one place before.
sentences.zh: 我不知道以前是否在同一个地方遇到过这么多松鼠和鸽子的喂养迷。

sentences.en: And although they agreed the animals should be eating healthy food,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们同意这些动物应该吃健康的食物，

sentences.en: they were not buying into the ecological model.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不买账这种生态模型。

sentences.en: The parks are not nature.
sentences.zh: 公园不是大自然。

sentences.en: They're an artificial situation.
sentences.zh: 它们是一种人工环境。

sentences.en: We are part of their environment.
sentences.zh: 我们是它们环境的一部分。

sentences.en: You can't change that.
sentences.zh: 这一点你改变不了。

sentences.en: When people expressed concern that certain animals in certain parks might starve,
sentences.zh: 当人们表达担心某些公园里的某些动物可能会挨饿时，

sentences.en: Gabriel tried to stand up for the hands-off approach.
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔试图捍卫顺其自然的方法。

sentences.en: The problem of them starving due to lack of food is because there's a higher population,
sentences.zh: 它们因缺乏食物而挨饿的问题之所以存在，是因为种群数量更多了，

sentences.en: because they're being fed.
sentences.zh: 因为它们一直被喂食。

sentences.en: It's a cycle.
sentences.zh: 这是一个循环。

sentences.en: But the applause was tepid.
sentences.zh: 但掌声寥寥。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It was not as poorly received as the founder and director of the Wild Bird Fund.
sentences.zh: 他的待遇还没有野生鸟类基金会创始人兼主任那么糟糕。

sentences.en: She was also against feeding.
sentences.zh: 她也是反对喂食的。

sentences.en: I would think the proposed amendment to the rule must also...
sentences.zh: 我想对规则的拟议修正案必须也...

sentences.en: She was actually booed.
sentences.zh: 她实际上被嘘了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, I ran over.
sentences.zh: 对不起，我超时了。

sentences.en: Exactly what effect the blanket ban would have on wildlife populations is unclear.
sentences.zh: 全面禁令对野生动物种群到底会产生什么影响尚不清楚。

sentences.en: But regardless of the ecological impact, the biggest takeaway from the hearing
sentences.zh: 但不管生态影响如何，听证会最大的收获

sentences.en: was that the concept of the more-than-human community, that was still going strong.
sentences.zh: 是人类以外社群的概念依然强劲。

sentences.en: I'm here today as a voice for New York City's non-human residents
sentences.zh: 我今天来这里是作为纽约市非人类居民的代言人，

sentences.en: because I see what's happening to our wildlife neighbors as really, truly tragic.
sentences.zh: 因为我看到我们的野生动物邻居正在遭遇的事情真的是一场彻头彻尾的悲剧。

sentences.en: The feeling that these animals are fellow citizens and should be treated with the same consideration
sentences.zh: 这些动物是同胞公民、应该受到同样关照的这种感觉

sentences.en: has never fully gone away.
sentences.zh: 从来没有完全消失过。

sentences.en: It is not just about what we want.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎我们想要什么。

sentences.en: It's about what the squirrels and all of the other-than-human beings in our parks want, too.
sentences.zh: 这也关乎松鼠以及我们公园里所有其他非人类生命想要什么。

sentences.en: And they are constituents of New York City.
sentences.zh: 它们也是纽约市的选民。

sentences.en: I go to the park every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都去公园。

sentences.en: People love to feed the animals in the park.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢喂公园里的动物。

sentences.en: On any park bench in any city, you'll see people throwing crumbs to the birds
sentences.zh: 在任何城市的任何公园长椅上，你都能看到人们向鸟儿

sentences.en: and the birds approaching for more.
sentences.zh: 抛洒面包屑，而鸟儿则凑过来索要更多。

sentences.en: We feel a connection to nature.
sentences.zh: 我们感受到了与大自然的联系。

sentences.en: For just a moment, both human and animal are doing something together.
sentences.zh: 就在那一瞬间，人和动物共同做着某件事。

sentences.en: That shared experience between species,
sentences.zh: 物种之间那种共享的经历，

sentences.en: that's what the people at the hearing didn't want taken away.
sentences.zh: 正是听证会上人们不愿被剥夺的东西。

sentences.en: Gabriel Willow also believes that there is value in connecting with these animals.
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔·威洛也相信与这些动物建立联系是有价值的。

sentences.en: But he sees it as a reason not to feed them.
sentences.zh: 但他认为这正是不要喂食它们的理由。

sentences.en: I think people really crave a direct interaction and connection with nature.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们真的渴望与大自然进行直接的互动和联系。

sentences.en: And so what I was saying when I spoke was like,
sentences.zh: 所以我当时发言时想表达的是：

sentences.en: look, please go to the park, observe wildlife, feel that connection.
sentences.zh: 听着，请去公园，观察野生动物，去感受那种联系。

sentences.en: You don't need to touch them.
sentences.zh: 你不需要触摸它们。

sentences.en: You don't need to pet them.
sentences.zh: 你不需要抚摸它们。

sentences.en: You don't need to hold them.
sentences.zh: 你不需要抱着它们。

sentences.en: You don't need to feed them.
sentences.zh: 你不需要喂食它们。

sentences.en: Like, it's actually more interesting and more valuable to stand back
sentences.zh: 我觉得，站在远处

sentences.en: and see an animal exhibiting a more natural behavior.
sentences.zh: 看一只动物展现出更自然的行径，其实更有意思、更有价值。

sentences.en: Watch a squirrel long enough and you'll see it play tricks on other squirrels.
sentences.zh: 只要观察松鼠足够久，你就会看到它捉弄其他松鼠。

sentences.en: If a squirrel carrying an acorn believes it's being watched,
sentences.zh: 如果一只带着橡果的松鼠觉得自己被监视了，

sentences.en: it will dig a hole, pantomime putting the acorn in the hole,
sentences.zh: 它就会挖个洞，假装把橡果放进洞里，

sentences.en: and then cover the hole back up,
sentences.zh: 然后再把洞填上，

sentences.en: all while hiding the real acorn in its mouth,
sentences.zh: 同时把真正的橡果藏在嘴里，

sentences.en: just to throw its fellow squirrels off the scent.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了转移其他松鼠的注意力。

sentences.en: Squirrels have been seen carefully organizing their acorns by size and shape
sentences.zh: 有人曾看到松鼠在埋藏橡果之前，

sentences.en: before they bury them.
sentences.zh: 会按大小和形状仔细将它们分类。

sentences.en: Biologists believe it's a mnemonic device that helps the squirrels remember
sentences.zh: 生物学家认为这是一种助记手段，能帮助松鼠记住

sentences.en: what they buried where.
sentences.zh: 什么东西埋在了哪里。

sentences.en: They have a specific call when they see a predator.
sentences.zh: 它们在看到掠食者时会发出特定的叫声。

sentences.en: So if you learn a little bit of squirrel language,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你学一点松鼠语言，

sentences.en: like, I know the hawk call, so if I hear that,
sentences.zh: 比如，我知道鹰的叫声，如果我听到那个，

sentences.en: I'll look up and often see a hawk.
sentences.zh: 我就会抬头，通常就能看到一只鹰。

sentences.en: So for them to just sort of allow us to be there,
sentences.zh: 因此，对它们来说，只是允许我们在那里，

sentences.en: but go about their day-to-day life,
sentences.zh: 却依然过着它们日常的生活，

sentences.en: is so much more powerful for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说这种感觉要震撼得多。

sentences.en: There's more than one way to connect to the animals with whom we share our cities,
sentences.zh: 与我们共享城市的动物建立联系的方法不止一种，

sentences.en: whether it's listening to the yipping of coyotes in the middle of the night,
sentences.zh: 无论是听深夜土狼的嗥叫，

sentences.en: setting up a webcam for the hawk nest outside your window,
sentences.zh: 为窗外的鹰巢架设网络摄像头，

sentences.en: or counting all the squirrels in Central Park.
sentences.zh: 还是数一数中央公园里所有的松鼠。

sentences.en: In March, Jamie Allen and the other team members of the squirrel census
sentences.zh: 3月，杰米·艾伦和松鼠普查的其他队员

sentences.en: finished gathering their data.
sentences.zh: 完成了数据收集工作。

sentences.en: They plan to reveal the squirrel abundance number in June.
sentences.zh: 他们计划在6月公布松鼠的数量。

sentences.en: Etienne Benson says he doesn't know how many squirrels there are in Central Park,
sentences.zh: 艾蒂安·本森说他不知道中央公园里有多少只松鼠，

sentences.en: but he thinks he does understand why everyone is so eager to find out.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得自己确实明白为什么每个人都这么急于弄清楚。

sentences.en: You know, one of the appeals of a squirrel census
sentences.zh: 你知道，松鼠普查的魅力之一

sentences.en: is just the same appeal that has existed since the 1850s,
sentences.zh: 正是19世纪50年代以来一直存在的魅力，

sentences.en: which is it's clear to people that the world around them
sentences.zh: 那就是人们清楚地看到，他们周围的世界

sentences.en: is not only inhabited by humans,
sentences.zh: 不仅有人类居住，

sentences.en: that it is this multi-species place.
sentences.zh: 它还是一个多物种共存的地方。

sentences.en: And I think there is a need and a desire there
sentences.zh: 我想那里有一种需求和渴望，

sentences.en: to know something about your neighbors.
sentences.zh: 想要了解一些关于你邻居的事情。

sentences.en: The census is a form of appreciation,
sentences.zh: 普查是一种欣赏的形式，

sentences.en: a way of recognizing that the squirrels are there.
sentences.zh: 是一种承认松鼠存在的方式。

sentences.en: And that, in itself, is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 而这本身就很美好。
